title: Sephiria Bosses — Erma & Final Boss (Qliphoth) Guide
description: Sephiria boss guide: Erma the Mad Scientist phases, golem hitboxes and laser dodges, plus final-boss (Qliphoth line) notes with Steam patch cross-checks.
meta: Erma (Mad Scientist) fight notes and final-boss notes for version 1.0, with sources. Covers sephiria bosses / sephiria erma / sephiria final boss searches. Page does not publish HP, timings or Pantaxis patterns.
body:
Two fights on this page: Erma, the Mad Scientist (the first wall most runs hit) and the final boss (Qliphoth line). Pattern notes are community-reported and cross-checked where possible; patch-tuned numbers should be verified in your client.

FightWhereStructureSignature patternWhat answers it
Erma, the Mad ScientistFloor 3, library line · Steam achievement “This Is Not Stalking”About three phases; she pilots a golem whose head and hands are separate hitboxesHands park top and bottom and scrape lasers while the head sprays; the two lasers move at different speedsWide AoE that clips several parts; any status applied to a part counts for the whole; high-damage runs delete the head first
Pantaxis, Guardian of the LibraryFloor 3, from Chapter 2 onward — can replace ErmaAlternate occupant of the same slot, not an extra fightNot covered in the notes below yetSame slot rules apply; treat any Erma habit as untested here
Qliphoth lineLate chapters, story climaxMulti-stage; patch-tuned numbers move between buildsCovered in its own section belowVerify timings in your own client after a patch

What this table is: a side-by-side of the two fights on this page plus the one that shares Erma’s slot, built only from the notes already published below and their cited sources — not from a fresh playthrough. Rows marked “not covered yet” are honest gaps, not summaries.

Erma, the Mad Scientist — Floor 3 / library line

Erma is the Floor 3 / library-line boss (Steam achievement “This Is Not Stalking”). From Chapter 2 onward she can be replaced by Pantaxis, Guardian of the Library.

Fight structure (NamuWiki cross-check)

  • About three phases involving a golem Erma pilots.
  • Golem head and hands have separate hitboxes—wide attacks that clip multiple parts deal more effective damage.
  • When golem HP depletes, Erma becomes targetable; deplete her HP to advance phases.

Key pattern note — dual lasers

Hands park top/bottom and scrape lasers across the arena while the head sprays. The clean dodge is to dash in the moment both lasers overlap and move the same direction (speeds are unequal). If tanky, sitting in the safer band and eating minimal chip can be better than panicking.

Weaknesses

  • AoE that hits multiple parts.
  • Status effects applied to any part count for the whole (freeze on a hand freezes the head; burns scale hard).
  • High-damage runs often just delete the head first when full AoE is awkward.

Final boss — the Qliphoth line

The story climax sits in the late chapters around the Qliphoth fight line. Steam patches after 1.0 explicitly tuned final-boss readability (bullet density, warning indicators, Hard Mode clear flags).

  • Expect multi-phase pressure; community clear videos often melt phases with stacked burn/frost/scythe setups.
  • Use official patch notes when something “feels wrong”—several patterns were hotfix-adjusted in mid-August patches.

How to read the table above

The table is a preparation sequence, not a difficulty ranking. “Where” tells you whether the fight sits on the story climb or shares a slot with another boss. “Structure” tells you how many phases to budget for. “Signature pattern” is the attack the notes spend the most words on. “What answers it” is the only column that should change what you pick up before the floor — if you read one column, read that one.

Main path and the fight that shares the slot

Erma sits on the story climb, at Floor 3 on the library line, and the notes here treat her as the first wall most runs hit. Pantaxis is the alternate occupant of the same slot from Chapter 2 onward. That distinction matters more than it looks: a slot-sharer is not extra content to prepare for, it is the same checkpoint answered by a different kit, and this page has no pattern notes for it.

For scale, the bosses guide cited below counts more than ten unique encounters across six chapters, with one mandatory boss per chapter and optional named fights alongside. It lists the Qliphoth fight among the optional named ones and treats the Chapter 6 ending fight as a separate encounter; this page uses “Qliphoth line” for the late-story climax as a whole. The sources do not settle the naming, so treat the label as a search term and confirm which fight you are in before relying on a note.

Before you enter

  • Commit the run first. One weapon branch and one or two Artifact families, chosen before the floor rather than at the boss door — the builds page lists the routes people actually finish.
  • Bring the answer, not the rarity. The table’s last column names what the fight rewards — wide AoE and status application for Erma — and an Artifact outside an active pattern wastes its slot, as the Artifacts and Tablets page explains.
  • Check the Side Bag before the door. Stored items are inactive, Tablets included, so a backup plan parked in the bag is not a plan (beginner guide).
  • If you run summons, let them tank. The Companion build uses pets as the aggro line while you finish elites and bosses, which is the job Erma’s separated hitboxes create.
  • Pre-load the Wishing Fountain with the family you intend to lean on (Wishing Fountain), but do not build the plan around a Bond Artifact: Steam players report those are not offered there.
  • Heal and reshuffle first. The bosses guide cited below reports no recovery rooms during the final boss gauntlet, so the state you enter with is the state you fight in.
  • Re-read the patch note if something feels wrong. Several patterns were hotfix-adjusted in mid-August patches, and the same guide records 1.0.21 changes to hitbox leniency and projectile counts on the Qliphoth fight, plus clearer telegraphs on the ending fight.

Common mistakes

  • Preparing for Pantaxis by rehearsing Erma. Same slot, different kit, and this page explicitly has no notes for it.
  • Building single-target damage into a multi-part boss. Head and hands are separate hitboxes, so a wide attack that clips several parts out-damages a focused rotation; the documented fallback is deleting the head first, not grinding the body.
  • Holding status effects for a perfect moment. A status applied to any part counts for the whole — freeze on a hand freezes the head — so an early application still buys the phase.
  • Dodging the dual lasers on reaction alone. The notes describe unequal speeds; the reliable window is the moment both overlap and travel the same direction, and dashing early walks you into the second beam.
  • Assuming the back half of a fight plays like the front. The bosses guide cited below puts most phase changes near half health, which is why the structure column exists at all.
  • Reading the table as a boss tier list. It compares preparation, not difficulty; nothing in it ranks one fight above another.

Which note carries which kind of evidence

Question you are askingWhere this page answers itHow firm the answer is
Is this fight on the story path?“Where” columnNamed from the Steam achievement and cross-checked against a wiki entry; the chapter counts come from the bosses guide cited below
How many phases should I budget for?“Structure” columnApproximate — the wiki cross-check says “about three”; treat it as a planning number, not a count
Which attack ends runs?“Signature pattern” column and the dual-laser notesCommunity-reported, cross-checked against recorded runs
What do I bring?“What answers it” column and the weaknesses listWiki weaknesses plus what community clears actually used
What does Pantaxis do?Nothing on this pageDocumented gap — the row says so
Exact HP, damage or timingsNothing on this pageNot published in any cited source, and nothing here estimates them

Each row maps to text already on this page or to one of the cited sources. The last two rows are gaps rather than summaries: if a number is missing, it is missing on purpose.

What these notes cannot tell you

  • Exact HP values or phase thresholds. None are published here, and none are inferred from the videos.
  • Frame data. No startup, recovery or invulnerability windows are given for any attack; the laser note describes relative speed only.
  • Pantaxis patterns. The table row is a placeholder, not a summary.
  • A phase count for the Qliphoth line beyond “multi-stage”.
  • A build requirement. Community clear videos melt phases with stacked burn, frost or scythe setups; that is an observation about those runs, not a gate. The scythe they use is a Dagger conversion, covered on the scythe page.
  • Anything about party play. Four-player runs add revives and shared loot; see co-op and multiplayer setup.

Questions the notes answer directly

Is Pantaxis a second Floor 3 boss?

No. It is the alternate occupant of the slot Erma holds, from Chapter 2 onward — the same checkpoint with a different kit, not an additional fight.

Does a freeze on the golem’s hand affect the head?

Yes, per the wiki cross-check: a status applied to any part counts for the whole golem, so cold on a hand also holds the head, and burn damage compounds from a single application.

What is the cleanest way through the dual lasers?

Dash in the moment both lasers overlap and move the same direction. Their speeds are unequal, so a dodge timed to one beam can leave you inside the other. Tanky runs can also sit in the safer band and eat minimal chip rather than panic-rolling.

Do I need a specific build to finish the story?

Nothing on this page requires one. What the notes support is narrower: wide AoE and status application answer Erma’s separated hitboxes, and community clears of the late fights used stacked elemental setups. Treat builds as options and the fight notes as the test.

Why does the final boss feel different after a patch?

Because it was tuned. Steam patches after 1.0 explicitly adjusted final-boss readability — bullet density, warning indicators, Hard Mode clear flags — and later hotfixes changed hitbox leniency and telegraphing again. Verify timings in your own client rather than against a video from an earlier build.

Where does Hard Mode fit?

Hard Mode is a separate unlock rather than a boss variant chosen at the door; the Hard Mode page covers the Chapter 2 route and the Root’s Retreat stages the achievements track.
